title: A completed-to-condensed coefficient realization at one scheme
statement: Let l be prime and X a Noetherian scheme on which l is a unit in global sections. There exists a CompletedRealization l X as defined in [def-sfb-diagonal-coefficient-reference]: an additive exact equivalence from completed coefficient modules to modules over the pulled-back condensed Z_l ring, with its underlying abelian-sheaf comparison and the prescribed regular-module finite-projection and integral-root-line normalizations. This assertion concerns one scheme and no direct-image functor.

source.place: paragraph (1); initial coefficient and supported-source identification, expanded in lem-diagonal-completed-frame proof

proof.text: Obtain the coefficient-ring isomorphism fixed by every finite reduction and the already constructed integral root map. Obtain the linear root-line isomorphism for this coefficient identification.

Compose scalar restriction along the ring isomorphism with the inverse internal/sectionwise module equivalence. Construct the inverse scalar restriction explicitly, with identity round trips on sections. Additivity follows on sections for reconstruction, hence for its inverse and the composite. As an equivalence the composite preserves finite limits and colimits. Its underlying-sheaf natural isomorphism is the reconstruction counit.

The inverse ring map gives an explicit sectionwise regular-module isomorphism. Lift its composite with the reconstruction counit through the fully faithful reconstruction functor; similarly lift the sectionwise root-line isomorphism. For either lift, applying reconstruction gives exactly the counit followed by its sectionwise comparison. Composing with the inverse underlying counit cancels the counit. Thus the unit normalization is the ring projection equation and the line normalization is the prescribed root map. Assemble these data into CompletedRealization.

proof_origin.place: paragraph (1), explicit scalar restriction/reconstruction and counit cancellation; coefficient-ring and root-line comparisons isolated as strictly smaller steps
